name: FWF Intercontinental Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: Awarded, not won: the federation put twelve men in a battle royale on another promotion's card, Dreamcard IV, and gave the last man standing a new championship. Blue Steele was that man, lost the belt to a backroll press with the ropes for leverage, and took it back with the Iron Deathlock. Three reigns across two men is the whole of its ledger, and the federation kept a separate five-man contenders list for it — an undercard division with its own ranking, run by the same hands.
notes: Transcribed from the federation's own singles ledger (promotions/fwf-1992/archive/fwf-singles-record-1993-01-08.html).

name: FWF Tag Team Championship
epitaph: Decided by an eight-match round-robin tournament its own ledger opens with, and won in the final by Storm, who broke one man's back and put another in hospital on the way there. Devastation took the belts off them in November 1992 with a cast to the back of the head, turned back the Chameleons, and then lost them at the Clash of the Masters to the PWA's own champions on a fall taken with a foot on the bottom rope and the referee not seeing it. The federation's own rankings, posted a fortnight later, still list Devastation as champions.
notes: Transcribed from the federation's own tag ledger (promotions/fwf-1992/archive/fwf-tag-rankings-history-1993-01-07.html). SOURCES DISAGREE on where the championship stood at the end: the same document records the Clash of the Masters loss and heads its own rankings "Champs: Devastation". Both readings are recorded.

name: FWF United States Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: The consolation prize of the founding tournament and the busiest belt on the ledger: six reigns across five men, with a vacancy in the middle when its holder won the World Championship and had to give it up. Damien Flayer held it twice, John Lawless twice, and Joe Reed took it off Flayer with a small package on 9 April 1992. Titan Morgan's win over Lawless on 14 October 1992 is where the ledger leaves it; a month later he defended it to a double countout and then carried it into the Clash of the Masters against the PWA's own United States Champion, and lost by countout.
notes: Transcribed from the federation's own singles ledger (promotions/fwf-1992/archive/fwf-singles-record-1993-01-08.html).

name: FWF World Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: The federation's top belt, and the one it opened with: its own ledger's first two matches are a double-elimination tournament, and the winner of the first was awarded the World Championship while the loser took the United States title as consolation. Five reigns follow across the ledger's own sixty-eight matches. Doctor Death took it first and lost it to a man who hit him with a stick; Annihilus won it by submission and lost it to an inside cradle; Titan Morgan held it until Death took it back with the Vulcan Death Grip on 15 April 1992, the one change of it the surviving record holds a report of. By January 1993 the federation was billing its holder as "PWA/FWF World Heavyweight Champion" — the belt had been unified with another federation's at the Clash of the Masters, and Death had won that too.
notes: Transcribed from the federation's own singles ledger (promotions/fwf-1992/archive/fwf-singles-record-1993-01-08.html).
